parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/routes.ts is an Express HTTP adapter in the infrastructure layer. Each handler does transport work only: it pulls fields from req.body, req.params or req.query, checks that the request has the right shape (required fields present, items is an array), calls a use case, and turns the result or error into an HTTP status and JSON body. Shape checks like these belong to transport, not to business rules. Nothing in the file decides how orders behave (state transitions, stock, pricing). The GET /api/orders/:orderId handler calls deps.orderRepository.getById directly instead of going through a use case. That is a plain read with a 404 mapping, not a misplaced business rule, and whether the route should depend on the repository is a dependency question that is out of scope here. Persistence logic, domain rules and framework wiring all stay where they belong.
